purpose: Targeted follow-up of 19 unresolved IDNrG assessments; authored primary check notes, not public-source archives.

checks.title: Addressed IDNrG land-register draft
checks.identity: Canonical 11-page Regelungsentwurf; PDF creation 20 July 2026; existing historical repository copy
checks.read_extent: Physical 1–3 and 6–11 fully re-read in this follow-up; not a new full 11-page read. Operative changes, cost model, implementation and special rationale.
results: Adds land-register datasets to IDNrG and restricts storage/use in land-register specialist systems. No express municipal specialist-software change.

Initial matching failures require no further action; inconsistent matched data are retained additionally with immediate effort treated as negligible. Ongoing inconsistencies are separately modelled at 5% of 2.4 million changes, two minutes each.
The net annual time saving is 4.8 million minus 240,000 minutes, or 76,000 hours; at EUR 43.20 this is EUR 3,283,200. One-off implementation estimate EUR 4 million.
limits: These are design assumptions and model estimates, not measured future outcomes. Generic IDNrG quality procedures may produce indirect work. Whether additional statutory initial reporting/review is fully priced is not established by the arithmetic.
checks.retention: Concise authored check note retained; new public downloads/extractions/renders are temporary until root and peer checks finish.

checks.title: AdV principles for dabag, ALKIS and LEFIS interfaces
checks.identity: Version 1.1, 10 April 2025; 76 physical pages; URL directory dated June 2026
checks.read_extent: Selected physical 11, 14–17, 24, 29–30, 33–35, 39 and 45–47; not the complete 76-page document. Physical 24 and 33–35/45–47 independently revisited before freeze.
results: Existing systems exchange structured data. The planned dabag model uses source/object IDs, including references to person objects; these are not a demonstrated lifelong natural-person tax-ID key.

Asynchronous/historical records require preprocessing; failed automated successor searches can require manual intervention. Person-to-person links are maintained in ALKIS preprocessing; ownership data include person and address objects, with opportunities to reduce redundancies and use newer addresses.
limits: A specification is not proof of nationwide implementation or measured error frequency. The explicit failed-successor example concerns parcel history; it corroborates a rework mechanism, not a measured owner-error project-delay effect. No equivalence between an object reference and unique identification of the same natural person across all registers is inferred.
checks.retention: Concise authored check note retained; new public downloads/extractions/renders are temporary until root and peer checks finish.

checks.title: Promulgated eNoVA Act
checks.identity: Act of 22 June 2026, BGBl. 2026 I No. 192, promulgated 26 June 2026; 14 pages
checks.read_extent: Physical 8–9 (including Articles 8 and 10) and 14 Article 20(5); cover/identity. No full 14-page read claimed.
results: Articles 8 and 10 create tax-purpose enquiry routes when required IDs are not already otherwise known. Article 20(5) conditions commencement on respective technical and organisational readiness and requires BMF to announce the respective date in the Federal Gazette.
limits: The promulgated conditional clause does not independently reconstruct the complete later announcement history or establish that no date had been determined by 7 August. October availability and an August undetermined date are different propositions.
checks.retention: Concise authored check note retained; new public downloads/extractions/renders are temporary until root and peer checks finish.

checks.title: Bundestag committee report on eNoVA
checks.identity: BT 21/5806, 6 May 2026; 20 physical pages
checks.read_extent: Identity physical 1; relevant operative query wording physical 6; complete explanations for new Articles 8/10 physical 17 and commencement explanation physical 18. Other sections not fully read.
results: The rationale expressly recognises cases in which clients have not supplied the tax ID; the new query is designed to enable the required transmission in those cases. The same rationale distinguishes property, deceased, donor and acquirer purposes.
The commencement explanation says technical connection work is still required and ties the query provisions to readiness.
limits: Pre-author primary legislative recognition of missing IDs supports non-universal possession, not a measured frequency of missing IDs, not universal ignorance in isolated land charges, and not the August announcement history.

checks.title: Primary tax-notification clauses
checks.identity: Current individual statutory clauses retrieved 26 October 2026; contemporary exact future-query provisions checked against June Act separately
checks.read_extent: Complete relevant individual clauses: GrEStG 18 and 20, ErbStG 34, ErbStDV 7, EStDV 54. Not all tax legislation or amendment history.
results: The obligations are transaction/purpose-specific, not a universal tax-ID field for every conceivable notarial deed. ErbStDV distinguishes mandatory deceased details from some details required only insofar as known.

EStDV 54 concerns corporation-related instruments and company tax numbers; it does not by itself establish a general natural-party tax-ID duty. Current GrEStG 18 contains electronic-filing changes and is not silently treated as the August procedural version.
limits: No exhaustive audit of every statutory basis across all notarial services. Current consolidation has post-response procedural changes; only scoped content is corroborative, with June promulgated text providing dated evidence for query design.

checks.title: Notarial identification and public-document proof rules
checks.identity: Current BeurkG 10 and ZPO 415/418 individual clauses
checks.read_extent: Complete three short individual clauses; no full statute/commentary or matching case-law survey.
results: BeurkG 10 requires careful personal identification and recording its basis or doubts; it does not universally prescribe a tax ID. ZPO 415 and 418 distinguish proof of recorded proceedings/facts, permit contrary proof, and condition facts outside own perception.
limits: These rules do not by themselves establish a regular evidential preference for older land-register data over later base data. No matching primary decision establishing the author’s proposed regular first appearance was recovered.

checks.title: AO tax-ID processing limits

checks.title: AO account identification obligations
checks.identity: Current AO 154 individual clause
